changed.title: The shortest optimal family of binary linear fingerprints has (2^m-1)/(2^gcd(m,s)-1) seeds for s output bits
changed.statement:
∀ (m s : ℕ), 0 < m → s ≤ m →
  let N := 2 ^ m
  let K := 2 ^ (m - s)
  let divisor := 2 ^ Nat.gcd m s - 1
  let period := (N - 1) / divisor
  let hits := (K - 1) / divisor
  let X := Fin m → Bool
  let Y := Fin s → Bool
  let collisions := fun (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → X → Y) (u v : X) =>
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin r => f i u = f i v)).card
  (∃ family : Fin period → X → Y,
    (∀ i, Function.Surjective (family i)) ∧
    (∀ i u v, family i (fun j => xor (u j) (v j)) =
      fun out => xor (family i u out) (family i v out)) ∧
    ∀ u v : X, u ≠ v → collisions period family u v = hits) ∧
  ∀ (r errors : ℕ) (f : Fin r → X → Y), 0 < r →
    (∀ u v : X, u ≠ v → collisions r f u v ≤ errors) →
    r * (K - 1) ≤ errors * (N - 1) ∧
    (errors * (N - 1) = r * (K - 1) →
      period ∣ r ∧ ∀ u v : X, u ≠ v → collisions r f u v = errors)
changed.unlocks: attains the finite collision threshold for split parity verification with shared randomness
changed.context: Let g=gcd(m,s). Regard the m-bit field as a vector space over its 2^g-element subfield. Fix a projection onto s/g coordinates. Precompose with multiplication by one representative per nonzero subfield-scalar orbit. On a fixed nonzero difference, exactly the kernel's nonzero orbits collide. For the converse count ordered collisions inside the output fibers. Balanced fibers minimize their sum. At equality every distinct pair has the same count. Reducing (2^(m-s)-1)/(2^m-1) gives the required seed divisor.

changed.title: A four-state boundary scan preserves agreement on the integer line and carries the XOR of the two boundary bits after certain misses
changed.statement:
let mix := fun (x : Int → Bool) (z : Int) => xor (xor (x (z-1)) (x z)) (x (z+1))
let evolve := fun (x injection : Int → Bool) (z : Int) =>
  xor (xor (mix x z) (!(mix x (z+1)) && mix x (z+2))) (injection z)
let run := fun (initial : Int → Bool) (inject : Nat → Int → Bool) (origin : Int) (n : Nat) =>
  (List.range n).foldl (fun (st : (Int → Bool) × Int × Nat × Bool × Bool) tick =>
    let x := st.1
    let b := st.2.1
    let mode := st.2.2.1
    let u := st.2.2.2.1
    let v := st.2.2.2.2
    let near := x b == !(xor u v)
    let far := x (b-1) == v
    let hit := mix x (b-1)
    let aligned := ((mode == 1) && near && far) || ((mode == 2) && far) ||
      ((mode == 3) && near)
    let diagonal := !hit && (((mode == 1) && !near && !far) ||
      (mode == 2) || (mode == 3))
    let nextMode : Nat := if aligned then (if hit then 0 else 2) else if diagonal then 3 else 1
    let f := b-3+(hit.toNat : Int)+((aligned && hit).toNat : Int)
    (evolve x (inject tick), f, nextMode,
      xor (mix x (f+1)) (inject tick (f+1)), inject tick (f+2)))
    (initial, origin, 0, false, false)
∀ (n : Nat) (origin : Int) (x y : Int → Bool) (i j : Nat → Int → Bool),
  (∀ z ≤ origin, x z = y z) →
  (∀ t < n, ∀ z ≤ origin+1, i t z = j t z) →
  let a := run x i origin n
  let b := run y j origin n
  let edge := a.2.1
  let mode := a.2.2.1
  let u := a.2.2.2.1
  let v := a.2.2.2.2
  edge = b.2.1 ∧ mode = b.2.2.1 ∧ (∀ z ≤ edge, a.1 z = b.1 z) ∧
    (mode ≠ 0 → u = b.2.2.2.1 ∧ v = b.2.2.2.2) ∧
    (mode = 1 → ¬ (a.1 (edge+1) = !u ∧ a.1 (edge+2) = !v)) ∧
    (mode = 2 → a.1 (edge+2) = v) ∧
    (mode = 3 → xor (a.1 (edge+1)) (a.1 (edge+2)) = !(xor u v))
changed.unlocks: Gives the transported boundary invariant for the four-state raw-key decoder.
changed.context: Induct on rounds. The nonlinear term in the second boundary output can fire only at the exceptional pair (b XOR c,1 XOR b). An aligned case excludes it. On a miss the initial boundary output is affine in the initial unknown bit. If the opposite partner of the exceptional pair is excluded, the firing indicator agrees with the initial unknown bit up to a fixed sign. XOR the two outputs to cancel it. Store that parity. Every remaining ordinary move excludes the usual pair. All parameters used in an active case come from the agreed interval.

changed.title: An XOR of disjoint degree-r products needs one linear query per product to lower the degree on any branch
changed.statement:
∀ (p r : ℕ), 0 < p → 2 ≤ r →
  let W := Fin p → Fin r → Bool
  let add := fun (x y : W) (row : Fin p) (col : Fin r) => xor (x row col) (y row col)
  let diff := fun (f : W → Bool) (direction point : W) =>
    xor (f point) (f (add point direction))
  let top := fun (f : W → Bool) (v : Fin r → W) => (List.ofFn v).foldl diff f
  let blocks := fun (word : W) =>
    (List.ofFn (fun block : Fin p => (List.ofFn (word block)).all id)).foldl xor false
  ∀ (lower : W → Bool), (∀ v x, top lower v x = false) →
    let observed := fun (input : W) => xor (blocks input) (lower input)
    let signed := Finset.univ.sum (fun sample : W => if observed sample then (-1 : ℤ) else 1)
    let linear := fun (n : ℕ) (q : W → Fin n → Bool) =>
      ∀ x y i, q (add x y) i = xor (q x i) (q y i)
    let drops := fun (n : ℕ) (q : W → Fin n → Bool) (base : W) =>
      ∀ (v : Fin r → W) (x : W), q x = q base →
        (∀ t i, q (v t) i = false) → top observed v x = false
    Int.ModEq ((2 : ℤ) ^ (p + 1)) signed ((2 : ℤ) ^ p) ∧
    (∀ c query, linear c query → ∀ base, drops c query base → p ≤ c) ∧
    (∃ query, linear p query ∧ ∀ base, drops p query base)
changed.unlocks: bounds the number of linear questions needed to lower the degree of disjoint products
changed.context: Expand the signed sum as a product of (1-2m) over Boolean monomials. Selecting t monomials covering u bits contributes (-2)^t 2^(pr-u). Modulo 2^(p+1) only covers by p disjoint degree-r terms survive. The original has exactly one. Change affine coordinates to make the branch a coordinate slice. If degree falls there, every top term meets a fixed coordinate, so p disjoint ones need at least p fixed bits. Reading one bit per block attains p. Allow 60 minutes. A gate-saving companion cannot exist for the number of queried linear bits.

changed.title: A binomial tail excludes every rematching, line flip and pooled OR decoder on one hard table
changed.statement:
∀ (n q e : ℕ),
  let I := Fin n
  let Table := I → I → Bool
  let loss := fun (G : Table) (q : ℕ) (π : Equiv.Perm I) (rowFlip colFlip : I → Bool)
      (R C : Fin q → Finset I) (out : Finset I → (Fin q → Bool) → Bool) =>
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (I × I)).filter (fun z =>
      out {z.1,z.2} (fun j => decide (z.1 ∈ R j ∨ π z.2 ∈ C j)) ≠
        Bool.xor (G z.1 (π z.2)) (Bool.xor (rowFlip z.1) (colFlip (π z.2))))).card
  let colors := 3^q
  let small := n/colors
  let rem := n%colors
  let pairs := (colors-rem)*Nat.choose small 2 + rem*Nat.choose (small+1) 2
  n.factorial*(2*colors)^n*(∑ j ∈ Finset.range (e+1), Nat.choose pairs j) < 2^pairs →
    ∃ G : Table, ∀ (π : Equiv.Perm I) (rowFlip colFlip : I → Bool)
      (R C : Fin q → Finset I) (out : Finset I → (Fin q → Bool) → Bool),
      e < loss G q π rowFlip colFlip R C out
changed.unlocks: bounds the number of switched tables recoverable under all physical rematchings at a given error
changed.context: For fixed matching and ternary addresses, balancing the C loads minimizes the number of within-class pairs, leaving at least B. Select B of these pairs. For a uniformly random table their swap parities are independent fair bits on disjoint cell pairs. Line flips change each parity by the sum of two label bits, giving at most 2^n patterns. At most e failures have probability 2^(−B) times the stated binomial sum. Union over n! matchings, C^n addresses and the flip patterns. Allow at least 60 minutes.

changed.title: The affine discrepancy of two biased inner-product banks lower-bounds binary cost at every nonlinear gate count
changed.statement:
∀ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s →
  let k := 2*s
  let N := 2^k
  let V := Fin k → ZMod 2
  let dot := fun (x y : V) => ∑ j : Fin k, x j * y j
  ∀ (label : Fin N ≃ V) (Q R : V → ZMod 2) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) →
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (N+N) C →
    PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (fun i j =>
      decide (dot (label i) (label j) + Q (label i) + R (label j) = 1)) C →
    let b := C.gates.countP (fun g => g.inputs.length == 2)
    let t := C.gates.countP (fun g => (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
      xor (xor (g.op.eval [false,false]) (g.op.eval [false,true]))
          (xor (g.op.eval [true,false]) (g.op.eval [true,true])))
    ∃ (T : V ≃ₗ[ZMod 2] V) (a : V) (e : ZMod 2),
      (∀ x : V, dot x (T x) = 0) ∧
      3*N + ((Finset.univ : Finset V).filter (fun x =>
        Q x + R (T x + a) ≠ dot a x + e)).card ≤ b + 2*t + 4
changed.unlocks: prices disagreements between two independently biased banks at any nonlinear gate budget
changed.context: Use the charged constant-diagonal symmetric square of size q. Above half, the lifted vectors (x,1) span. Symmetry identifies the map x to (paired name,bias sum) with a single self-adjoint linear operator on those lifts. Its address block T is invertible. The constant diagonal makes x dot T x constant on more than half the cube. This linear form must vanish, making T alternating. The discrepancies lie outside the square. At or below half, exchange the two coordinate halves and choose the better constant. Estimate 120 to 210 minutes after the matching bound.

changed.title: When a cyclic window omits one bit, the maximum size of a minimal conflict equals cube size minus the minimum radius-one covering code size
changed.statement:
∀ (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n), 2 ≤ n →
  let Word := Fin n → Bool
  let Pat := Fin (n - 1) → Bool
  let V := Sum (Fin n) (Fin n × Pat)
  let Pin := PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Literal V
  let accepts := fun (a : V → Bool) =>
    ∀ i : Fin n, a (Sum.inr (i, fun j : Fin (n - 1) =>
      a (Sum.inl ⟨(i.val + j.val) % n, Nat.mod_lt _ hn⟩))) = true
  let fits := fun (pins : Finset Pin) (a : V → Bool) => ∀ l ∈ pins, a l.1 = l.2
  let core := fun (candidate : Finset Pin) =>
    (∃ a, fits candidate a) ∧ (¬ ∃ a, accepts a ∧ fits candidate a) ∧
    ∀ e ∈ candidate, ∃ a, accepts a ∧ fits (candidate.erase e) a
  let covers := fun (centers : Finset Word) =>
    ∀ x : Word, ∃ c ∈ centers, (Finset.univ.filter (fun k : Fin n => x k ≠ c k)).card ≤ 1
  ∃ (P : Finset Pin) (S : Finset Word),
    core P ∧ (∀ l ∈ P, ∃ i : Fin n, ∃ p : Pat, l = (Sum.inr (i, p), false)) ∧
    (∀ Q, core Q → Q.card ≤ P.card) ∧ covers S ∧
    (∀ T, covers T → S.card ≤ T.card) ∧ P.card + S.card = 2 ^ n ∧
    (3 ≤ n → 3 * 2 ^ n ≤ 4 * P.card) ∧
    ((∃ r : ℕ, n + 1 = 2 ^ r) → (n + 1) * P.card = n * 2 ^ n)
changed.unlocks: It gives the obstruction size for the propagation-depth criterion when the window misses one bit.
changed.context: Replace each word pin by forbidden row entries, preserving one private word per old pin. A pattern missing one coordinate excludes the endpoints of one cube edge. A minimal edge cover is a spanning forest of stars. Its centers dominate. Conversely assign vertices to a minimum dominating set and shift a leaf to any isolated center, or augment if its neighbor is a center. Three-bit faces give two centers per eight words. At Hamming lengths, syndrome-zero words tile the cube by radius-one balls.

changed.title: Exact line count and degree of binary polynomial calculus refutations for signed graph clauses
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (left right : Fin m → Fin n) (sign : Fin m → Bool),
  let cl := fun (e : Fin m) (a : Bool) =>
    ({(left e, !a), (right e, a ^^ sign e)} : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause (Fin n))
  let negative := fun k : ℕ =>
    ∃ (v : ℕ → Fin n) (edge : ℕ → Fin m), v 0 = v k ∧
      Odd (((Finset.range k).filter (fun j => sign (edge j) = true)).card) ∧
      ∀ j < k, (v j = left (edge j) ∧ v (j+1) = right (edge j)) ∨
        (v j = right (edge j) ∧ v (j+1) = left (edge j))
  let P := MvPolynomial (Fin n) (ZMod 2)
  let ax := fun (e : Fin m) (a : Bool) => PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.clausePoly (cl e a)
  let legal := fun (t : ℕ) (p : Fin t → P) =>
    (∃ root, p root = 1) ∧ ∀ i, p i = 0 ∨ (∃ e a, p i = ax e a) ∨
      (∃ v : Fin n, p i = MvPolynomial.X v * MvPolynomial.X v + MvPolynomial.X v) ∨
      (∃ j < i, ∃ k < i, p i = p j + p k) ∨
      (∃ j < i, ∃ v : Fin n, p i = MvPolynomial.X v * p j)
  ∀ g : ℕ, negative g → (∀ k < g, ¬ negative k) →
    ∀ L d : ℕ,
      (∃ (t : ℕ) (p : Fin t → P), t ≤ L ∧ legal t p ∧ ∀ i, (p i).totalDegree ≤ d) ↔
      4*g ≤ L+1 ∧ (if g = 1 then 1 else 2) ≤ d
changed.unlocks: determines the exact line count and attainable degree for binary polynomial calculus on signed edge clauses
changed.context: Trace the constant one back to its premises. Boolean axioms and zero vanish on every Boolean word, so the selected clause inputs alone must be unsatisfiable. The weighted core at unit cost forces at least 2g inputs, which need at least 2g−1 binary joins. For distinct endpoints the two clause polynomials sum to X_u+X_v+sign. Sum both blockers around a shortest negative cycle, cancelling every variable, to get one. A negative loop has two opposite unit polynomials. All inputs have degree at least two when g>1, apart from zero. Allow at least 60 minutes.

changed.title: Minimum inconsistent signed edge clause cores pair all clauses by complementary private words
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (left right : Fin m → Fin n) (sign start : Fin m → Bool),
  let oddSet := fun D : Finset (Fin m) =>
    Odd ((D.filter (fun e => sign e = true)).card) ∧
    ∀ v : Fin n, Even ((D.filter (fun e => left e = v)).card +
      (D.filter (fun e => right e = v)).card)
  let W := Finset.univ.filter oddSet
  let faults := fun x : Fin n → Bool =>
    Finset.univ.filter (fun i => x (right i) ≠ (x (left i) ^^ sign i))
  let missed := fun x : Fin n → Bool =>
    (faults x).filter (fun i => x (left i) = start i)
  (∀ x, (missed x).Nonempty) →
    (∀ (i j : Fin m), i ≠ j →
      ((∃ x, faults x = {i,j}) ↔ (∀ D ∈ W, i ∈ D ↔ j ∉ D)) ∧
      ((∃ x, faults x = {i,j}) → ∃ y, faults y = {i,j} ∧ missed y = {i} ∧
        missed (fun v => !(y v)) = {j})) ∧
    ∀ g : ℕ, m = 2*g → (∀ D ∈ W, g ≤ D.card) →
      ∃ mate : Fin m → Fin m, Function.Involutive mate ∧
        ∀ e, mate e ≠ e ∧ ∃ word, faults word = {e, mate e} ∧
          missed word = {e} ∧ missed (fun v => !(word v)) = {mate e}
changed.unlocks: recognizes pairs of complementary private assignments in signed clause selections of minimum size
changed.context: A two-fault word solves the linear edge equations with two signs toggled. The parity solvability criterion tests this on every dependency. Testing odd dependencies suffices, since each even one is the difference of two odd ones. Under complementation the two faulty equations persist and each selected blocker switches truth, forcing one private violation per word. At the minimum every active coordinate is balanced and every odd dependency has size g. Pair opposite-offset occurrences of each linear part. A gate-saving companion cannot exist for complement pairs of private clause assignments.
